annotation.material_differences: B and C add an explicit policy/authorisation safeguard: they say compensation may be available but must be passed to the right queue or routed appropriately if the speaker cannot approve it. A only says to route through the normal process if compensation looks supported, without the same clear limitation on personal authorisation. This could change the policy-awareness assessment under CSS03-C2.
annotation.equivalence_rationale: A, B, and C all share the core evidence pattern for CSS03-C1 and CSS03-C3: they review account/incidents/location, avoid a premature refund decision, and continue investigating or update the customer when evidence is inconclusive. However, B and C preserve stronger evidence of respecting authorisation limits and escalation procedures, while A is less explicit about that constraint. Because the presence or absence of an authorisation safeguard is decision-relevant under the stated criteria, the responses are not fully equivalent.
